newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat sets new highs on flooding.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat sets new highs on flooding.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures were higher at midsession and new contract highs were notched in the deferred months on growing concern about flooding in key spring wheat growing areas, traders said.
"It is just basically flood concerns," one floor trader said.

North Dakota congressman Earl Pomeroy said Sunday about 1.7 million acres of North Dakota cropland were under water due to flooding and much of that acreage will not go into agricultural production this growing season. North Dakota is the leading U.S. spring wheat growing state.
The new high for new crop September is $4.79-1/2 a bushel, above the previous high of $4.70 set on July 12.
At 1200 CDT, MGE spring wheat futures were 6-1/4 to nine cents per bushel higher, with May up 7-1/4 at $4.71. New crop September was up 7-1/4 at $4.70-1/2.
